utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Meanwhile, one preliminary matter resulting from yesterday, and if the Prosecution doesn't mind, I'll take the lead. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution has uploaded under number 65 ter 02370A the excerpts from the transcript of the 26th Republika Srpska Assembly Session, which was tendered with Witness Radojica Mladjenovic. I refer to the transcript page 27105, on the 21st of October. Already provisionally number P06838 was assigned, and the Chamber now understands that where it was announced that page 124 and 25 would be tendered, that it is page 1, page 24 and page 25. [The witness takes the stand].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6838 is admitted into evidence and if there's any problem with the excerpts, the Defence has an opportunity to raise it within the next 48 hours. Good morning, Mr. Savkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I do understand that you have received again the documents you've given yesterday to the Tribunal. Now, if you want to consult any of these documents, and there were six, then you should first ask for permission and tell us which document you would like to consult. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I also would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Stojanovic will now put his last two questions in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have 699 in e-court, please. D699. And could we focus on paragraph 32 of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in paragraph 32, you speak about information that you received, that the Muslims were preparing an all-out attack on Vlasenica in order to take control of it and establish their own government. Could you please tell the Court how it was that you received this information?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite by accident, if I can put it that way. The cleaning lady at the municipal assembly, the lady who was cleaning the office of the president of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica, a diary was found, and as far as I can remember, the date was the 13th of April, and his notes were found under that date, and it was quite clear from that what it was that was being prepared by the SDA. That is one thing. Another thing: People who were as worried as we were provided information to us. That's the second reason, actually. On the 20th of April in Cerska, a unit was lined up, and its commander and command were proclaimed, and the leader was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However the previous document was more important, the one that I told you about. And it was clear on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I seek clarification, Mr. Stojanovic, if you don't mind. Sir, you are quoted here as saying the cleaning lady and then you say a diary was found and his notes. Whose notes are these? Whose diary was this? It's obviously not the lady's because now it's a male who owns it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The diary was of the president of the Executive Council of the municipality of Vlasenica, Izet Redzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The information doesn't come from the lady. The president of the assembly already had the information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The president of the Executive Council, in his diary, under the date that I mentioned, he kept notes, and everything was clear, on the basis of those notes, what was being prepared. If you put that up on the screen, I can provide further comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not necessary. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just -- did you see that diary, or did the cleaning lady just relay that information to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to me. She relayed it to people who lived up there in Vlasenica in that period. And who worked with us, who were in this council for interethnic co-operation or, rather, the people who were working on that agreement that we spoke about yesterday. And, of course, all of this took its own line afterwards towards the MUP and the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But my question mainly focuses on did she take those notes and show them to those persons, or did she look at it and then told these others what the content was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She showed it to them and she gave them the diary. And not only the diary but also a page on which it was written further up "the herd to be killed," and then a list of the best known Serbs from the entire municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you happen to have a copy of that page, or do you know where a copy can be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I brought that copy to my lawyer, and I brought it to the trial of Mr. Radovan Karadzic. It was admitted into evidence in the Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so on and so forth. It's been used for a long time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I see Mr. Stojanovic is nodding yes. Does that mean that you want to tender that Mr. Stojanovic or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour. That is my next step.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But for the transcript, could the witness be clear on the position that Izet Redzic held at that point in time. You say that these are his notes.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Izet Redzic was the president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica; there's no denying that. That is to say, that he exercised power together with his co-workers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Line 2, on page 3, I think there's a bit of a difference. I think there's a bit of a difference in the answers in the transcript so that's why I asked this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have another document, 65 ter 1D03503.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness -- actually, have you ever had an opportunity before of seeing the handwriting of the then-president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He worked in the same company where I worked. That is to say, the bauxite mines, Milici. He was an engineer, a mechanical engineer, that is to say, he worked in a different department because I worked on an electrical maintenance. After all, we went to high school together as well. The first grade of high school. This is his handwriting, absolutely. However, as far as I know, he never denied it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: With your leave, in view of what this document looks like, I'd like to ask you something. The upper part is typewritten --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What's this about?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a copy of that page from the diary that was published in the gazette or, rather, a gazette that was being published then. I think it was called Glas Birca. So on page 2, you can see a photocopy of this diary page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in this part of the text on the right-hand side underneath the date, the 13th of April, 1992, this is what is written: "The commission worked well, given the conditions?" And then the next line: "Herd for slaughtering." Now this line, is that what you were telling us about a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's one of the things that was there. It said "herd for slaughtering" and then there was this list. I mean, the most prominent Serbs. Or, how do I put this? Well, I'm not saying the intelligentsia, but the most prominent Serbs in the entire municipality of Vlasenica. Milici was included as well. For example, I think I was the third person on this list. That's what they told me. I haven't seen this list though. Because it is well known where it ended up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber, to the best of your recollection, where did this list end up?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original of this page was taken by then-Colonel or Lieutenant-Colonel, Radovan Tacic. He was from the armoured unit. Actually he said that he would take this institute, and so on and so forth, somewhere in Belgrade or Uzice. When 40 tanks were being withdrawn, he was a commander there. He took that to Serbia and this court and the other courts and prosecutor's offices of Bosnia and Serbia should find Mr. Radovan Tacic. He's still alive and he would have to know where this is. However many people had seen this. One of the people who had seen this was a witness who testified here in the case of Radovan Karadzic, Zoran Zivanovic was his name; unfortunately, he is deceased. His brother was the seventh person on that list. A young man, a high school student who lived a modest life. To this day, he did not understand why he was on that list, and he did see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, now could you tell us, you said that it clearly appears that a number of Serbs would be killed after a take-over, a massive attack on Vlasenica. Could you tell us exactly where you find the attack and where you find the clear indication that Serbs would be killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two points, and I will -- actually, there are three points, and I will tell you. If you move onto the next one: "Call the president of the Municipal Assembly of Tuzla, Beslagic, to address our refugees." And then the next one is: "The General Staff is directing the entire operations." And then most importantly, focus on the left-hand side underneath these names. This is what is written --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... go to the next page in English. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Isko, to let out the children from the secondary school for Friday and Monday. Secure a motive and inductor from Finale." The Friday was supposed to be the 24th. That's easy. Well, inductor from Finale and then get the children out of the secondary school there can only be two motives. One is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does it say at all, I mean, apart from motives. He see that Isko is to let out the children from secondary school on Friday and Monday. Which suggests that they go there on Friday and they go there on Monday. What is so clearly indicated here that ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, sir, it's quite clear. Inductor from Finale. Inductor. That's equipment that any army in the world would have. That is for dealing with explosives. One is to take the Muslim children out because he is referring to them and then the remaining Serb children should be kept there and blackmailed, or blown up using this inductor. Isko is Isko Jasarevic. He is an officer. Later on, he was appointed assistant commander for morale at the Cerski detachment. In the chronicles of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you can find his CV, and it says that I figured prominently in the training activities of the Patriotic League in March 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand what so clearly emerges from this document. That is what I'm focussed on at this moment rather than on background information you may have. Where does it say that this will be an attack on -- on Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said this, what is here, and this is what I'm saying now. I'm going back to -- well, actually we're on the same page. We're on the same page. On the right-hand side. What is written here and it should be translated, "organised for defence" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in English could we have the first page of the document again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So underneath this, above the names, actually, it's stated very clearly: "Organisation for defence". In all of their documents when they speak about attacks against our villages and the like, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I have some difficulties in understanding that the words "organising for defence" is a clear indication of attacking Vlasenica. I mean, I may understand that you may have this interpretation. But you said it clearly appears from this document, which, by the way, seems to be a kind of cut-and-paste document anyhow. But I am trying -- you said there are two things are clear. First, an attack on Vlasenica, and, second, a list of Serbs to be killed. Now these two items I'm trying to see where the document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- unambiguously states that. And you've told us that the attack should be deduced from three persons being charged with organising for defence. Now, the Serbs to be killed, where do we find that in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that it is on this list "the herd for slaughtering," and I said where that list is right now. However, I've also stated that, as far as this Isko is concerned and the preparations of this sabotage, it is quite clear anywhere in the world, in any army, what someone does with an inductor. Starting with any soldier, the lowest ranking sergeant, up to a general. Or even a high school student. Everyone know was an inductor is used for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- let me just see whether I fully understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you can explain what you understand to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In all formations of the world, in all armies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm asking you what you understand to be an inductor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An inductor is a device that is used, most often, in engineering, or in construction companies, or companies that are involved in destruction by the use of explosives. Electrical networks are set up with explosives. Then this becomes a very powerful induction generator of electricity. If you've watched American films and other films, then it has this handle up here, and then when the explosive is activated, you either press it or you twist it; it depends on the manufacturer. And in this way, the explosive is activated. As an engineer, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Stojanovic, apparently this is important part of what you present as evidence. The translation of the document says something quite different. Because it talks about a doctor rather than an inductor and, therefore, I'm a bit confused that you didn't check that part of the -- of the evidence. And the translation. Because...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in English again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because that's where it appears. It says: "Isko to let out the children from the secondary school for Friday and Monday. Secure" - and then it says something that difficult to - "engine and doctor from," it reads "Isola" but I did understand that you said "Finale". Can you read what kind of a -- what kind of a machine or engine has to be secured? So the words before inductor, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking the witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does it read? Could you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says clearly: And I-n-d-u-k-t-o-r. You can't see the I at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the word before that. So the last word on the fourth line --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Ensure M-o-t" and then the next letter could be O and then R which means motor. Then again, it could be M-o-t, which is quite clear, but the rest is not so clear. If we take this to be motor then it goes very well with the next word, "inductor".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that a motor inductor? And how do we have to -- how do we have understand a motor inductor to be related to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the word motor, there is a word "and", "motor and an inductor". A motor and an inductor from Finale. That's the name of the company that is in wood processing and other businesses. There was never a doctor in Finale, and the word inductor is the same as in this sentence. It's Monday and Friday. And you can see that it's identical as that which is before the word inductor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is an inductor a component which is very broadly and generally used in all kind of technical equipment, I would say electronical equipment or electronic components of equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I am an electrical engineer and it doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say it doesn't exist. Let me just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm talking about an inductor. Is an inductor specifically a component of an explosive device or is it a generally used in many, many appliances, a kind of a small part of an electrical circuit which is used in many, many technical or electrical appliances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you are telling us that -- what doesn't exist? Does an inductor not exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Isko was a philosophy teacher and a reserve military officer. As for philosophy, there is nothing that you will find under the name of inductor. Whereas in the school for reserve officers, an inductor is the device that I described. That is the only thing that you come across if you attend a military school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I -- I do understand that an inductor is not the main subject in philosophy teaching. But I'm trying to find out how specific the reference to an inductor is for an explosive device. I mean, a motor, which apparently is also mentioned there, I wouldn't immediately think a motor to be necessary or to be specifically to be used for explosive activities. Now, I'm asking myself the same question for an inductor. Is an inductor a electronical or electric device specifically aimed at being used in explosive devices or is it a rather general electrical or electronical component which is used in, well, let's say, in washing machines, in radio equipment, in whatever. I'm trying to understand why I conclude from the mentioning of the word inductor that this is an exercise which is aiming at explosives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, why were only Muslim children taken out from the secondary school, and on a Friday, at that? Why? He was a reserve captain. Why the Muslim children?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please focus your answer --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the teacher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please focus on what I asked. And if you are unable to do that, then we leave it for that. Mr. Stojanovic, if you can shed some additional light and also on where the document reads that only Muslim children are to be let out from the school, not only on Friday, apparently, linked to explosions but then on Monday again which then comes a bit as a surprise. If you can shed light on that, together with the witness, you're invited to do that. But, first of all, always check the translation so that we are not thinking in terms of doctors, rather than in terms of inductors. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will do so, Your Honours. The translation of the document is the one that we had uploaded in the system, and we felt we were obliged to clarify this with the witness, and then we shall try to verify the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, at the time, that is to say, in mid-April 1992, what were relations on the ground like in municipality of Vlasenica? And I'm talking about interethnic relations.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, gentlemen, we were established or, rather, six of us were chosen as the most respectable people. We appreciated one another extremely, and we still have high regard for each other, especially while Dr. Dzana was the president of the SDA, we were able to keep the situation in Vlasenica under control, absolutely. However, the major problems occur in the exercise of power. For example, Izet Redzic was the president of the Executive Committee. There was no Serb who would approach this person in order to solicit any favours for me, and there were many reasons for that. This same person with whom we communicated but not only with him, there was also Sefo Saracevic, who was the secretary of the municipal assembly. There was also Mustafa Imamovic who was the president of the court. He would always feel somehow threatened and unable to exercise his power. At one point, he decided to arm all his associates, that is to say 21 of them and including the president of the municipality, and two porters, all of them had handguns both during working hours and after working hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a moment and let's focus in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we go back to the first page in English of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The man that you just described in terms of his conduct, if this is his handwriting and his words, says: "The General Staff will direct all the operations." I'm asking you: Did you have any specific knowledge about what kind of General Staff he was speaking that time, on the 13th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentleman, it's absolutely clear. At that time there was no Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, according to the Yugoslav constitution and the BH constitution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not what General Staff was not meant. The question was what General Staff is being referred to here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The General Staff mentioned here was the Main Staff of the Patriotic League, and it's quite clear who members of the Patriotic League were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how do you know that that is what is meant here? Is that your interpretation of the document, or do you have any specific reason to believe that that is what General Staff is referring to here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who among the Muslim people would be directing operations other than the General Staff of the Green Berets, et cetera. That's one thing. Secondly, yes, I did have knowledge. There were millions of facts that could be proved. Many of them were well known back then and today as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I leave it in the hands of Mr. Stojanovic what to select from the million -- millions of facts, because that might be a bit too much at this moment in the three minutes that were remaining for you, Mr. Stojanovic, approximately 45 minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will comply, Your Honours. Can we now look at paragraph 20 of your statement, D699, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is supposed not to speak aloud. He knows what the consequences will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 20 of your statement where you speak about the forming of paramilitary formations of the Patriotic League and HOS. When you were giving your answers a while ago, I just like to ask you specifically, did you have any concrete knowledge that in April of 1992 units of the Patriotic League and the HOS were already operational in Vlasenica and Birac?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just an example: In September, members of the Patriotic League were publicly lined up in Tuzla. I think it was in November, rather. Then, in Vlasenica, HOS or the Croatian Party of Right, General Pijukovic [phoen], members of HOS were walking around the village in broad daylight completely freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender document 1D03503 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness be asked to remove his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please -- first of all, do you understand the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I remove my earphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should first -- put them on again, please. You should first answer my question, whether you do understand or read the English language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't give you an answer. I can read a bit. I used to be fluent in English but nowadays -- I wouldn't say that I know the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the information you gave us is sufficient to not deal with the matter in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. President, it might be most expeditious I will have a few questions about the document and I'd just ask that it be MFI'd and we address it at the completion of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed in that way. Madam Registrar, the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3503 receives number D705, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. You are aware that you have put a few questions to the witness which - and you have put a document to the witness - which raises so many questions that you would have done better by starting with that issue rather than do it at -- in the last three minutes of your examination-in-chief. But please conclude soon your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now have D699 again, paragraph 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, just briefly, 42. Here you speak about a sabotage carried out by Muslim paramilitary formations on the 27th of May, 1992, and I'm going to ask you only what is the basis of your information that this event had occurred in the manner explained here.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw all this and experienced all this. This Court saw relevant documents during the trials of both Radovan Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik. There are criminal reports. There are perpetrators who committed the crime, and quite importantly, there is a number of Muslims involved there, including Mirsad Sulejmanovic. But I can give you many more names, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what is your personal knowledge about the perpetrators? So not what you learned from documents but do you have any personal knowledge about the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in Milici at the time. My company, Boksit was transporting ore from the pit to the foundry in Zvornik. The road ran through Konjevic Polje. It was a convoy made up of 30 vehicles. On the way back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I fully understand that you learned about the incident. My question was focussed on whether you have any personal knowledge about the perpetrators. Were you there, did you see them, how did you gain any information about who perpetrated this crime, as you told us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The survivors, the drivers. One of them was a neighbour of mine, Milan Dukic. We drew up together. We were born in the same village of Dubnica. He told me everything. We had been living next to all those people until recently, and you can find his statement about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. What is in his statement, we'll leave it to the parties to present that statement or not. What did he tell you about the perpetrators? What he saw when it all happened. Did he identify a perpetrator, or did he know the perpetrator? Could you tell us what he told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He told me everything. How they set up an ambush. He was one of the lorry drivers. He mentioned specific people whom he recognised among other -- the man known as Taran. So you can find other names in his statement. I personally cannot remember them at the moment, but if I were to see his statement, it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We're not going to give that you statement at this moment. Do I understand that what you have read in his statements is what he had told you. Is that more or less how we have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He first related this to me, and then later on, he gave a statement to the public security station in Milici. So he was one of the persons with whom I had this kind of conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the content of the statements, to the extent you are aware of them, are the same as what he told you. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'll finish with one more question. Did you have an opportunity to attend a funeral of any of the employees from the company where you used to work, who were the victims of these tragic events?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately, rarely. In May of 1992, we would have buried someone each and every day. If we started to go day by date, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'm not going to insist on this any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with this, I have concluded my examination-in-chief, and, therefore, I will not tender this document that you pointed out as a witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's not tendered then. We've five minutes left. Perhaps -- Mr. Traldi, apparently it was relevant for the admission of the other document. Is there any way that you could start with that and see if we can deal with that before we take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm not sure I will complete that line but I'll make a start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see where it ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find him to your right and Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir you were asked some questions this morning about a document that you identified as part of Izet Redzic's notebook. When was the first time you saw that document?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was sometime between the 16th and 18th of April, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you mean in 1992?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is the document, yes, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, beginning on the 14th of April, 1992, you had, in fact, left Vlasenica and gone to Milici; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 13th of April. The session of the municipal assembly was held on the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, that's not what I asked you. What I asked you was: Beginning on 14th of April, you had left Vlasenica municipality, you had gone to Milici municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I live in this place called Milici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you went at that point in time from Vlasenica to Milici. Whether you lived there or not is a different matter. Sometimes people are at a place where they do not live. Did you go at the point in time mentioned by Mr. Traldi from Vlasenica to Milici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I live there. I spend my nights there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you were no longer in Vlasenica when this document was, as you said, discovered by a cleaning lady; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was travelling every day as a member of this council. Apparently you haven't read the agreement. I literally travelled from Milici to Vlasenica every day, and then further on to Sarajevo. I cannot account for every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there. My wife was there. My mother-in-law was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir, I've asked about the 14th because of your own previous testimony in the Krajisnik case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31466, page 105.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take it you testified truthfully in that case, to the best of your knowledge. That's your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in the middle of this page, the Defence counsel is asking you about Muslims who had left Vlasenica. He says: "What was the effect of the Muslim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Line 14, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "What was the effect of the Muslim departures that you have described?" You say: "The departure of Muslims instilled fear into everyone, Serbs and Muslims alike." You speak for a few more lines. And then on line 21, after describing some rumours, part of which was propaganda maybe, you say: "But I cannot tell you more about it because already on the 14th I was in Milici; I was not in Vlasenica." So, in fact, you can't tell us more from your personal knowledge about what was happening between the 14th and the 20th of April in Vlasenica, because you were already in Milici; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you asked me whether I had any knowledge about what you had asked me about. I could have that knowledge in Milici as well, just like in Vlasenica, and at the mine, and so on and so forth. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I stop you there. You're moving subject. Whether you could have known anything being in Milici is a different matter. What Mr. Traldi puts to you is that, today, you tell us that you went up and down from Milici to Vlasenica, whereas, in this other case, you testified that you could not know what happened in Vlasenica because you were in Milici, which clearly suggests that you were not, on a daily basis, in Vlasenica. That contradiction is what Mr. Traldi is asking you about. Do you have an explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't even say that. Rather, this knowledge, I answered that my knowledge about this was up until the 18th. I didn't say where. Well, of course, you can ask me but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that -- if that's your explanation, then Mr. Traldi will put his next question to you. But only after the break, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take the break first, and you're invited to follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to come in, I already have two small questions, Mr. Stojanovic, about the document which is MFI'd at this moment. First of all, in the translation, it -- in the top line, it refers to a number, 12, whereas, in the -- in the translation, it's appendix number 16/, a slash I do not find in the original. And, second, an appendix to what is, of course, one of the questions that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- may be in need of an answer. We'll continue, Mr. Savkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, continuing with questions about this notebook page. During your testimony in the Krajisnik case, you didn't mention it at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some other light, yes, yes. I must have. I cannot remember right now. I testified for all of five days. However, in the meantime, I remembered some very important things that you have in this transcript that is very important for the Court as well. More or less, all my knowledge related to Vlasenica, I gained from Radomir Bjelanovic, a personal friend of mine, who was chief of the public security station at the time. That's what I told you, knowledge. Basically from him I heard about the situation in Vlasenica and beyond at any given moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was it him who told you about this purported notebook entry?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think now -- well, no, it's not that I think. Perhaps further on in the transcript. In most places, well, certainly -- now whether he actually told me about this, probably, because he was there on the spot. And this is exactly what he did in operative terms, and the public security station in Vlasenica. At that time he was chief of the public security station in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to focus your answer on the question I ask you. So I take it that you do not recall now whether it was Mr. Bjelanovic who told you about this notebook entry. Have I correctly understood your answer, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the information that is important from the public security station of Vlasenica, I had all of that, as I talked to my family friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that you're not certain whether you -- whether Mr. Bjelanovic told you about the notebook entry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two men, Radomir Bjelanovic and perhaps Zoran Zivanovic, but I think it is Radomir Bjelanovic. I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not certain. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, given this time distance whether I'm sure or not sure ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no one blames you for you. But we'd like to know whether you know or whether you just think or whether you're not certain. That's the issue and you're not blamed in any way for not remembering certain matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you heard from one of those two men, you didn't see the original document at the time it was discovered, did you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The original ... now was it the original or not? I don't wish to say that. I don't wish to state whether I saw the original or a copy. It is certain that I did see it in that period though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You don't know, then, if anything was added to it after it was discovered, do you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw is that, what was on the screen. All of these important things that I talked about, I saw them then. And then I understood it as I said today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you again to focus on the question. Between the time it was discovered and the time you first saw it, you don't know whether anything was added to the document as it was found; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question? I don't think that the interpretation is good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You don't know whether anything was added to the document between the time when it was found and the time when you first saw it, do you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period of a few days, of course, I don't know whether something was added or not. How could I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in April of 1992, the Muslim holiday Bajram fell that month; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Muslims slaughter animals for feasts for Bajram; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in terms of organising for defence, in early April 1992 there had been conflict in Bijeljina and Zvornik, hadn't there?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And doesn't it stand to reason that people in municipalities near there would be concerned about conflicts spilling over into their areas and want to defend themselves?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us were more concerned in that period because of the Croatian army that entered Posavina, and everything that was done to the Serbs by the regular Croat army in the area between Brod, Derventa and Modrica. So it was both Serbs and Muslims. Those would come later. Because this had been going on for already a month and a bit more than that and that situation affected us a lot more, both of us, because we both saw that there is no state, that the state cannot protect us. And that is why we sat down to reach agreement. Now what you are trying to say about Bajram, Kurban Bajram, it was on the 4th of April and on this page, sir, the first item is quite clear. Our work is being assessed and in the first item -- bring it back and you will see. Commission worked well on the basis of the conditions that it worked in. Given the conditions it worked in. And that commission could only have been from the 13th onwards. So you take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, again, you've confirmed that you don't know what was in the document when it was found and what was added later, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have confirmed that. I've confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to complete my questions in this area, I'd put to you that you were asked in the Krajisnik case why the protocol fell apart. You answered for four pages, so I won't read the entire thing. You mentioned rumours, you mentioned speculation, you mentioned propaganda. You did not mention this notebook entry. So I'd put to you that you, in fact, learned of this notebook entry between your testimony in the Krajisnik case and today, not in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it is absolutely easy to refute what you're saying. Bring this back to the screen so that Their Honours can take a look at this. And you will see that that part is --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Glas Birca, Glas Birca, that paper from the third of March. So what you're saying just now is and I'll tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm stopping you. What the document says is a matter different from when you learned about it. What Mr. Traldi puts to you is the following, since you did not refer to this document in any way in the Krajisnik case, he infers from that and puts that to you, that you learned about this document only after your testimony. He is not stating that the document did not exist at that time but that you learned about it only after your Krajisnik testimony and gives you an opportunity to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The entire population of Vlasenica, Muslims and Serbs, were aware of that document. It was published in the newspaper Glas Birca. I have it in my own documentation and that one page we can see from that. So what you are saying is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 19819. I'm turning to a different subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision dated the 4th of April, 1992 establishing a Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica. This was signed on your behalf because you were in Tuzla with General Jankovic that day; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, not with General Jankovic. It was on the 3rd of April. I was with him on the 3rd of April whereas this list says the 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31468 page 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You've just been shown this same document in your testimony in the Karadzic case. Sorry, I have the page number wrong, I think. Could we try page 36, please. So you're being asked in a question that ends at the top of the page about this document. You say in line 4: "Just a moment. On the 4th of April, I have it somewhere in one of the paragraphs here. I was in Tuzla then" -- and the attorney questioning you referred you to a paragraph of your statement. But you said: "I'm trying to explain. It says the 4th of April. That's why my signature is not there. As for my paragraphs, there is somewhere where it says ... on the 4th of April, 1992, I was in Tuzla. I went to see General Jankovic. But there's nothing to be disputed. The 4th of April. You know that it is basically the beginning of the war." So your testimony in the Karadzic case was that this was signed for you on the 4th of April because you were in Tuzla with General Jankovic. Do you stand by that testimony today?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bad translation. Bad translation. I did not say that. But this is what I did say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you challenging what is -- okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it will be verified on the basis of the audio. If you say that my words were mistranslated into the Karadzic case. We'll get the audio ready, it can be listened to again, and we'll see whether there's any wrong translation. So if that's the issue we'll do that and there's no need to further explain unless ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You added --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, in the statement in Radovan Karadzic's trial and in my statement here, it is clearly stated that on the 3rd of April, I was in Tuzla with General Savo Jankovic. Take a look at both statements, and that's for sure. However, over here, when I saw this document obviously since I saw it for the first time, I mean, it was very quick, and it was in a hurry so I didn't notice that the month was April. Well, it's possible that I said that I was there then, but when I testified in Radovan Karadzic's case, and also in General Ratko Mladic's case, it is clearly stated that I was then in Tuzla with General Jankovic and this is the period. This is the period. Up there. That false heading of this decision that you, from the Prosecutor's office, tried to sneak in, while we are working on the agreement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can tell us about facts. Allegation and accusations can be put forward through Defence counsel. If you have told Mr. Stojanovic about any falsification, you certainly pay attention to it. But you are supposed to tell us about the facts and it may be clear that in your testimony in the Karadzic case and apparently you do not challenge that anymore, you told that the signature on the document was not there before because you were in Tuzla where you went to see General Jankovic. On the 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wrong, wrong --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it is correct that the signature is not mine and over here this was just -- this one moment I mean, made a mistake, the date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Signature is not mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no dispute about that, I think. If you make a mistake rather than think about that before you accuse our interpreters of giving wrong interpretations, yes? We'll not accept such behaviour any further. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You also testified about this document, "Let's be clear, the Crisis Staffs were formed whenever the situation was critical for the people." The Crisis Staff in Vlasenica was, in fact, formed on the 4th of April, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right. I don't know about that because from the 30th of March until the 11th of April, we, this group, was working on the agreement, the one that is attached here, and that was adopted by the assembly. Milenko Stanic and I and others were on this group, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Crisis Staff was formed on the 4th of April, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it not formed, or do you not know when it was formed, on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that meeting, even if it had been formed, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No one asked you whether you were there or not. You leave it open that it was formed on the 4th of April, if I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you -- but you do not know? Because if you know, tell us what date it was when it was formed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't even know when it was formed because I wasn't there. If it was formed. If it was formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness apparently doesn't know when a Crisis Staff was formed, if it was formed at all. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31468 receives --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19819 receives number P6839, Your Honours. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Mladic, one more loud word and you'll be removed from the courtroom. It's now two or three times today that you spoke aloud. You know exactly how to communicate with counsel without raising your voice, without speaking at a volume audible for others. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now in Milici municipality, there was a War Presidency in 1992, right, but you did not serve as a member?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was that? May or July? May 1992 or July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I suggested to you was that in 1992, in Milici municipality, there was a War Presidency of which you were not a member; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I think you've anticipated my next question. There was also a War Presidency in Milici municipality beginning in July 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was, but, actually, everything functioned as if it did not exist. There was still an assembly and an Executive Board but in accordance with the decision or order of Radovan Karadzic or the National Assembly, yes, it did exist and it was supposed to send reports every month, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then you were the president that time; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the assembly. The president of the assembly is, at the same time, the president of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 04480.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a report you sent in your capacity as president of the War Presidency on the 18th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could we have page 2 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Directing your attention to point 2, you write: "We trust that you are aware of the security situation in Milici municipality, but just to use an example, the last three times parts of Milici municipality and the surrounding area were combed, 35 Turks ... were killed and three were captured." So my question for you is: Was it common for you to refer to Bosnian Muslims as Turks in your official documents?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 4480 receives number P6840, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Staying with 1995 for a moment, in paragraph 76 of your statement, you describe how the bodies of Muslims who you say were killed in July 1995 crossing the Djugum-Kaldrmica-Konjevic Polje road were collected and buried in several graves along that road. I have a few questions about this aspect of your evidence. First, while you don't use the words Nova Kasaba, what you're describing is the road between Nova Kasaba and Konjevic Polje; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This area is near the border between the Milici, Vlasenica and Bratunac municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if Milici and Vlasenica is one municipality for you, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In 1995, Milici and Vlasenica were separate municipalities in the RS; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to re-ask my question. This is an area near the borders between Milici, Vlasenica, and Bratunac municipalities; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area between the municipalities of -- this is the area between the municipalities -- this is at war time. So it is between the Muslim municipality and the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31486.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while it comes up, Nova Kasaba, by establishment, was part of Milici municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, you saw that agreement, it's clearly stated that Nova Kasaba belongs to the municipality of Muslim Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we have partially that cleared. But since my colleague cannot follow English, the answer that starts on 36, page line 6, specially line 7 and 8 should be maybe clarified because that was not the answer the witness gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was recorded. So it is between the Muslim municipality and the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what the witness said, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is recorded as having said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But now he, in 36, 13 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- he explained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- let me just -- Witness, part of one of your answers was that Nova Kasaba is between the Muslim municipality and the municipality of Vlasenica. That's how it was recorded and interpreted for us. Is that correct or did you say something else? It is between what and what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nova Kasaba is a settlement that, when the division was carried out on the 13th of April 1992, came to belong to the Muslim municipality of Nova Kasaba. No, the Muslim municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was there a functioning government of the Muslim municipality of Vlasenica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July 1995, it did not exist in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an image that's been generated by our mapping unit based on internal data. For your orientation, we see Nova Kasaba at the bottom, the football pitch identified just north up the road, and then further up, there are two triangles identified as Nova Kasaba (1996) and Nova Kasaba (1999). Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nova Kasaba (1999), yes. No, that's not Nova Kasaba. There's the territory of Bratunac municipality. This stream that goes westerly from Svilile where these three houses are, constitutes a border between let's say Vlasenica and Milici. So this triangle indicating Nova Kasaba (1999) is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down and repeat the rest of his answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last part of your answer when you referred to Nova Kasaba (1999), you said that was ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the territory of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which municipality would the football pitch have been in?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This football pitch is, as I said, on the border but in the former single municipality of Vlasenica but after the division of 1992, it was allocated to the Muslim municipality of Vlasenica, and it's been recorded as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which functioning municipal government was governing that area in 1995? The Serb municipality of Vlasenica, or the -- or the municipality of Milici?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In actual fact, until the division in the post-war period, this was a no man's land. The Milici municipality ended far behind Nova Kasaba on the ridge called Kapava Stijena, although you cannot see it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the triangles that we see on the map reflect the two mass graves that the Office of the Prosecutor is aware of along this road where you've said those bodies were buried. Do they match your recollection as to where the bodies you were describing were buried?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you see written here, Nova Kasaba (1999), I've never seen this grave. I've never even seen it being excavated. As for the grave, it could have been there in the year 1996. It's a grave under the fly-over on the road where the armed forces of the 28th Division committed the major breakthrough towards Cerska and there were dead bodies left there. I suppose that the unit that carried out sanitation measures only dug out a grave near the stream and buried the bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, when it says 1996, you're aware, aren't you, that an exhumation was carried out in that area in 1996?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several exhumations there, and I cannot remember whether it was in 1996 or in some other year.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I move on, I'll tender this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31486 receives number P6841, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Could I ask you one question, Witness. You earlier said Nova Kasaba (1999). In that could not be Nova Kasaba because the stream there is the demarcation of -- now, looking at this map, would you agree with me that Nova Kasaba (1996), that triangle, is at the same side of that stream as Nova Kasaba (1999). The triangles are both situated to the east of the stream. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The triangles are as they have been plotted on, the triangles. Where this triangle is, there were houses before the war and there are still houses standing there. I don't know why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reason why I'm asking you this is because earlier when you said this could not be Nova Kasaba because of the stream being the border, that I understood that as a possible confusion that you thought that Nova Kasaba (1999) was at the other side of the stream compared to Nova Kasaba (1996), whereas, as I see them on this map, they're both on the same side of the stream, that is, the easterly side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. That's not the stream that I said. I told you that the border-line between the municipalities of Vlasenica and Bratunac, if you look to the right, Nova Kasaba (1999) you can see the word Svilile. Now look at this elevation to 1996. It descends and comes to the border between the municipalities. There are houses and a restaurant and therefore why this area is called Djugum after the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My concern about a misinterpretation have been removed. You referred to something different than I thought you did. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, since you suggested that the Nova Kasaba (1996) location might be the one you're talking about, I'd like to look at another exhibit, Exhibit P1834, page 32. And while it comes up, the substantive evidence explaining the locations that are represented by the triangles is found, for instance, in the evidence of experts Haglund and Baraybar. And page 32 of this document, please. It will be photographic so if we could just zoom in on the one page. Now, Mr. Haglund has analysed the graves exhumed in 1996 identified by the triangle you mentioned and discovered that 27 of the 33 victims found there were found with their hands tied behind their backs. Now this is a picture, in fact, it's two pictures of the one of the bodies exhumed at that location. You can see that his hands are bound; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd put to you that your evidence that the people buried along the road in these graves were killed trying to cross the road is false. That the great majority of them were found with their hands tied behind their backs and they were, in fact, captured and then murdered. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 13th of July, I passed along this road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What year? 13th of July what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1995. In this section to the right, towards Svilile and the rest of it, I saw dead bodies. I also saw behind the houses that I mentioned also I saw bodies which were in kind of fetus position but, sir, as president of the municipality I'd like to say something. During the breakthrough carried out by the 28th Division above Gornji Mratinci, two members of my former battalion were taken by the Muslims as prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- until this very day their fate is unknown. It is possible that these are two -- these two men. We are still searching for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean the two on the pictures could be those? Mr. Traldi, have these --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is possible. Nobody knows anything about what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you're telling us that it's possible that the people you lost may have been captured and may have been then killed and are the ones who are depicted here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not perhaps. They were captured and taken away. These are perhaps exactly these two. I suppose that DNA will be obtained from their family members. Do you want to hear the names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, has DNA identification been performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, on the victims in this grave have been confirmed to be Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we are not interested in your suggestions, in your allegations, your theories. These bodies, the DNA was taken from the bodies and they have been identified and they are not the men you suggest they are. Could you please stick to factual knowledge you have in answering any questions rather than to give room for your, what seems to be quite some imagination rather than knowledge of facts. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything I said is a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, one more such comment and we'll finish your testimony in this court because are you not here in a debating club. You're here as a witness and you should carefully listen to the questions and to the instructions given to you. Is that clear? You're called by the Defence, and we'd like to hear proper evidence as presented by the Defence, because that's as important for us as any other evidence, but just allow us to do it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, with that, I want to turn to your evidence about 1992. Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P188. This is a report from the East Bosnia Corps to the Main Staff dated the 7th of June, 1992. I'd direct your attention to point 8. In the English, I think we'll have to go to page 2. Here it reads: "In the area of Zvornik we have around 500 prisoners, and in the area of Vlasenica around 800." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At this point, June 1992, Zvornik and Vlasenica were in the East Bosnia Corps' area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the 7th of June ... 7th of June ... it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what we see here is functional communication from those municipalities up to the Main Staff about the prisoners being held there at that point; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read it all. If you allow me to read everything?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, all I'd asked you about was point 8, which was one sentence. Can I take it that you've finished reading that sentence?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Those 800 in Vlasenica were being held in Susica camp; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It doesn't say anything there. But I don't understand it. It says at the top, the 7th of June, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we agree that in June 1990, there was no Army of Republika Srpska and no East Bosnia Corps?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know nothing about the Eastern Bosnia Corps. I had too much business to take care of in the defence of the mine, so I don't know anything about it. Since it says 1990, that's the only thing I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you are not invited to comment on the date. This Chamber can see the date. The parties can see the date. You're asked about what is reported here, there being around 800 prisoners in Vlasenica, whether they were held in Susica camp in 1992, to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no knowledge about that, nor did I have any at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At this point, you weren't part of the East Bosnia's Corps' reporting structure to the Main Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You got it completely wrong. The 7th of June. As of the 1st of May until 18th July, we were constantly engaged in combat on the road leading to the mine. It can easily be remembered because, on the 10th of June, a village just before the mine was burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I think you've answered a different question that the one I asked. Let me try it this way. When you were the commander at the mine, who did you get your orders from?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was the commander of the defence of the mine, and I came there sometime after the breakthrough which would, say, on or about 18th of July, and that is when I arrived at the mine. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- witness, again, that's not the question. From whom did you receive orders at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, the brigade commander was last name Andric, I cannot remember his first name. However, with regard to the mine, I didn't receive orders from anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's the answer to the question which we would love to hear two minutes ago. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now could we have P6564.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an instruction by Branko Djeric then the prime minister of Republika Srpska to the Boksit mine to supply fuel to DD Romanijaprevoz in Pale, dated the 24th of May, 1992. So at that time the authorities in Pale had communication with the Boxsit company; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you'd better ask Mr. Dukic about this. He was the manager of Boksit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Boksit was the largest company in the area and employed about 3200 people; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Dukic was a member of the SDS Main Board and Executive Board; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is already the period when the Serbian Democratic Party suspended all its activities. It can be found in documents. I wasn't interested in that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stop. Stop you again. Was he a member of the SDS Main Board at that time, whether functioning or not is a different question. Was Mr. Dukic a member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that he was ever a member of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You apparently do not know but you think he was not. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Executive Board of the Serbian Democratic Party?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this period. I don't know how long he was a member of the Executive Board, which is a completely different thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P3735.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is the Vlasenica Serb Municipality decision appointing its War Commission. Do you see the date is the 16th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have P3046.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision by President Karadzic confirming the appointment of the members of the Vlasenica War Commission. Do you see the date is 17 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 17th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm showing you these documents because in paragraph 83 of your statement, you say: "We were unable to get in touch with the state and military leadership immediately because the communications were down and the roads were not passable." So I'd put to you that these documents show that your evidence in that regard was not truthful, that there was rapid and functional communication along both the military and political lines in June of 1992. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think, in all fairness to the witness, I think he should be shown paragraph 33 -- 83 so that he can see exactly and in its entirety what he said there before giving an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness would be shown paragraph 83, he can read it during the break and then the question will be put again to him after the break. Mr. Traldi, you quoted a portion of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
